# Atomic&lt;T&gt;

One value that threads read and change without a lock.

```rux
pub struct Atomic<T> {
    // private fields
}
```

`T` must be an integer of 8 to 64 bits, `bool` or a pointer; any other type is refused where the methods are used.
Shared by reference between threads; the value lives inside, so it must outlive every thread that reaches it.
Copying an `Atomic` copies its current value into a new, unrelated one.

## Type parameters

| Name | Description                                                        |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `T`  | the value's type: an integer of 8 to 64 bits, `bool`, or a pointer |

## Constructors

<h3 id="new"><code>Atomic</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Atomic(value: T) -> Atomic<T>
```

An atomic value holding `value`.
Making one is not itself atomic: it must be finished before another thread can reach it, as any value must be.

| Name    | Type | Description       |
| ------- | ---- | ----------------- |
| `value` | `T`  | the initial value |

**Returns**: an atomic holding `value`

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Atomic/Src/Atomic.rux#L30)

The current value, read with `order`, which must be `Relaxed`, `Acquire` or `SequentiallyConsistent`.
`Release` and `AcquireRelease` read as `Acquire` and `SequentiallyConsistent` respectively, the nearest orders a
load can have.

<h3 id="compare-exchange"><code>CompareExchange</code></h3>

```rux
pub func CompareExchange(
    self: &Atomic<T>,
    expected: T,
    desired: T
) -> T ! T
```

Replaces the value with `desired` if it is `expected`, as one step, with sequential consistency.
Succeeds with the value before, which is `expected`, when it replaced it, and fails with the value it found
otherwise, so a loop can retry from what is really there. Never fails spuriously.

| Name       | Type | Description                  |
| ---------- | ---- | ---------------------------- |
| `expected` | `T`  | the value that must be there |
| `desired`  | `T`  | the value to put there       |

**Returns**: the value before, as success when it was replaced and as failure when it was not

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Atomic/Src/Atomic.rux#L99)

<h3 id="compare-exchange-with"><code>CompareExchangeWith</code></h3>

```rux
pub func CompareExchangeWith(
    self: &Atomic<T>,
    expected: T,
    desired: T,
    success: MemoryOrder,
    failure: MemoryOrder
) -> T ! T
```

Replaces the value with `desired` if it is `expected`, with `success` when it does and `failure` when it does
not.
Orders a failure cannot have are strengthened to the nearest it can: `Release` reads as `Relaxed`,
`AcquireRelease` as `Acquire`, and a failure order stronger than the success order as the success order's
acquire part.

| Name       | Type          | Description                          |
| ---------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `expected` | `T`           | the value that must be there         |
| `desired`  | `T`           | the value to put there               |
| `success`  | `MemoryOrder` | the order when the value is replaced |
| `failure`  | `MemoryOrder` | the order when it is not             |

**Returns**: the value before, as success when it was replaced and as failure when it was not

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Atomic/Src/Atomic.rux#L117)

<h3 id="fetch-add-with"><code>FetchAddWith</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FetchAddWith(
    self: &Atomic<T>,
    value: T,
    order: MemoryOrder
) -> T
```

Adds `value` with `order`, wrapping on overflow, and returns the value before.
The relaxed form is what a counter whose value nothing else depends on needs. Only for integer `T`.

| Name    | Type          | Description                                     |
| ------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `value` | `T`           | what to add                                     |
| `order` | `MemoryOrder` | which other operations may move across this one |

**Returns**: the value before the addition

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Atomic/Src/Atomic.rux#L166)

<h3 id="fetch-sub-with"><code>FetchSubWith</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FetchSubWith(
    self: &Atomic<T>,
    value: T,
    order: MemoryOrder
) -> T
```

Subtracts `value` with `order`, wrapping on overflow, and returns the value before.
The release form is what dropping one reference to shared data needs, so that the last one sees every write
the others made. Only for integer `T`.

| Name    | Type          | Description                                     |
| ------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `value` | `T`           | what to subtract                                |
| `order` | `MemoryOrder` | which other operations may move across this one |

**Returns**: the value before the subtraction

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Atomic/Src/Atomic.rux#L183)

<h3 id="zero-int8"><code>Zero</code></h3>

```rux
pub const Zero: Atomic<int8> = Atomic<int8> { value: 0i8 };
```

An atomic `int8` holding zero, as a constant, so a module variable can start as one through an alias of
